items.title: 5 restaurants that opened in Mississauga, Oshawa and Niagara in September 2026
items.summary: A fresh mix of flavours arrived across southern Ontario this month, giving diners a few more places to add to their must-try lists. From Japanese ramen and Indian-inspired pizza to Turkish favourites and a new rooftop dining experience in wine country, the latest additions offer a little bit of everything. , Unit 11. The restaurant specializes in Japanese ramen made with slow-cooked broths and a variety of noodles and toppings. Established in Toronto in 2012, Kinton Ramen has grown to more than 60 locations across Canada. Its other Mississauga restaurant is on Confederation Parkway near Square One Shopping Centre. Terrain and The Rooftop opened at The Clayfield, a new Hyatt Unbound Collection hotel at 18 Clayfield Commons in Niagara-on-the-Lake. Terrain is an all-day restaurant highlighting local food, agriculture and Niagara wines. Menu items include East Coast scallop crudo, wild rice risotto, house-made lobster bucatini and dry-aged duck lettuce wraps.

items.title: Just Seven of 17 Ward 7 Hopefuls Show Up to Answer Voters' Questions in Mississauga
items.summary: According to a report from mississauga.com, only seven of the seventeen candidates running for Mississauga's Ward 7 council seat turned up for a public meeting where residents could question them directly. The Sept. 14 event, organized by the Applewood Heights and Hills Residents' Association, drew more than 30 attendees to the Royal Canadian Legion branch on Dundas Street. Topics ranged from crime and affordability to concerns over e-scooters in the ward. Adad, a former manager with Safe City Mississauga who spent a decade working in crime prevention and the non-profit sector, told the crowd he wants candidates to move past short-term election promises and focus on longer-term solutions. Alves, a former Peel District School Board trustee, argued that new housing developments in the area have not been planned with Ward 7 families in mind. The low turnout among candidates left many residents' questions unanswered by more than half the field seeking the seat. With the Oct. 26 municipal election approaching, voters looking for direct answers from candidates may need to seek out other forums before voting day.

items.title: Mississauga Opens Early Voting Options Starting Oct. 6 Ahead of Election Day
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents wanting to skip the lines on election day can start casting an early ballot on Oct. 6. The first stretch of advance voting, running Oct. 6 to 7, is limited to a single location at the Mississauga Civic Centre on City Centre Drive. Starting Oct. 8, advance polling expands to all 11 ward locations across the city, running through Oct. 11. Voters are not restricted to their own ward during this period and may cast a ballot at any available site. City officials note that this flexibility applies only during the advance voting window, not on election day itself. Voting day proper falls on Oct. 26, when residents must return to their assigned polling location. The expanded advance schedule gives Mississauga voters five extra days beyond election day itself to make their choice known.

items.title: Mayoral Debate Reveals Rare Consensus on a New Parking Garage for Troubled Ridgeway Plaza
items.summary: According to INsauga, the idea of building a four-storey parking garage behind Ridgeway Plaza came up Friday afternoon during Mississauga's first mayoral debate of the election season, held at Sheridan College's Hazel McCallion Campus. A moderator asked the four main candidates what they would do to make the west-end plaza, home to roughly 115 restaurants, more pedestrian and traffic friendly. Incumbent Carolyn Parrish, who won a mayoral byelection in June 2024 after Bonnie Crombie left for provincial politics, pointed to a large plot of land behind the plaza and said a paid parking facility there would pay for itself within three to four years. INsauga reports that while the four candidates, who also included city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, disagreed on most issues during the nearly two-hour debate, they largely agreed on building a new parking garage at Ridgeway Plaza. Crombie, who served as Mississauga's mayor from 2014 to 2024 before leaving to lead the Ontario Liberal Party, told the debate audience she is concerned for residents living near the plaza who have dealt with noise and other problems in recent years.

items.title: Peel Police Funding Formula Takes Center Stage as Parrish Claims Ford Committed to a Fix
items.summary: According to the Star, Mississauga's mayoral debate on Friday produced an unexpected claim from incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish about the future of Peel police funding. Parrish told the debate, hosted by CBC and the Mississauga Board of Trade, that she has convinced Premier Doug Ford to revisit a funding formula she says leaves Mississauga taxpayers covering an unfair share of policing costs compared with Brampton. She said she raised the issue directly with Ford at his home about six weeks earlier and that he agreed to act once the legislature returns in November. Parrish did not specify what a new formula would look like but said she would accept something closer to an even 50-50 split, rather than the current arrangement that puts roughly 62 percent of the cost on Mississauga. The claim followed criticism of her earlier decision to resign from the Peel police board, which she has defended as a response to what she called an unprecedented request for budget increases. Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown pushed back on the idea that the formula is unfair, pointing to costs Mississauga incurs related to Pearson Airport, which are partially reimbursed, and the regional marine unit. Parrish suggested Brown was avoiding the topic rather than addressing it directly.

items.title: Thousands of Salmon Push Upstream Through the Credit River as Mississauga's Annual Run Gets Underway
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, an annual salmon run is now underway in the Credit River, drawing thousands of fish swimming upstream from Lake Ontario in what the city calls an annual phenomenon. The city says the run typically begins each September in Mississauga, as well as in parts of Brampton and Caledon, and continues through the end of October, usually peaking in early October. INsauga reports that some of the best spots in the city to witness the event include Erindale Park, The Riverwood Conservancy's Riverwood Park and Meadowvale Conservation Area. According to the city, the salmon push against the current of the Credit River each late summer and early fall to spawn and lay their eggs. City officials explain that as water temperatures cool and fall rains raise water levels, freshwater salmon begin their yearly trek from the mouth of Lake Ontario up the Credit River to spawn. The city encourages residents of all ages to come witness the natural event for themselves.
